Hearts & Flowers.summary: Los Angeles folk-rock trio, including future Byrd Bernie Leadon, sitting right at the folk-to-country-rock hinge just before Sweetheart of the Rodeo.
Hearts & Flowers.related: Bernie Leadon; the Byrds; Dillard & Clark

Heatmiser.summary: Portland band pairing Elliott Smith's melancholic songwriting with Neil Gust's darker material, foreshadowing Smith's hushed solo direction.

Helena Deland.summary: Montreal songwriter whose graceful, literary indie folk pairs delicate acoustic arrangements with glittering Sam Evian production.

Helium.summary: Mary Timony's Boston band moving from fuzzed-out 1990s noise-pop into stranger, synth-driven art rock built around fairy-tale imagery.

Hem.summary: Brooklyn band applying slowcore's patience and hush to a lush, orchestral chamber-pop sound that found an NPR audience outside the indie underground.

Hiding Places.summary: Brooklyn-via-North Carolina band playing brutal, pounding riffs with dual lead vocals, the loudest, least twangy corner of the countrygaze scene.

Highway 101.summary: Los Angeles-based neotraditional country band fronted by Paulette Carlson's raw, twangy alto, anchoring the mid-1980s pushback against countrypolitan gloss.

Hiss Golden Messenger.summary: M.C. Taylor's Durham, NC project moving from private four-track folk recordings into a warm, Dead- and Band-indebted cosmic country-soul catalog.

Home Is Where.summary: Palm Coast, Florida band whose whirlwind hardcore aggression and harmonica-flecked folk melancholy fuse American Football-style emo with country and folk instrumentation.
